Arial goes through text_render::measure_with_family_and_face, which already selects ARIAL_FACES by bold and italic and falls through the font chain for characters outside the ASCII table. No new decimal literal. No label match. No SVG rewrite. Add a harness_guards test that rejects a match arm whose pattern is one or more string literals and whose body returns a high-precision float (3+ decimal places) inside shipping crate sources. No existing allow-list is edited. If that scan hits a legitimate site, the test is not added and the guard is reported as a proposal. A library assertion calls the public measurement path for the reference label and one held-out label. It does not branch on the label. Before removing the field, build a mutant of the Arial-fixed tree that passes false instead of font.bold and compare whole CLI output with the unmutated tip on every golden and perturbation. If that mutant is byte-identical (stdout, and exit status; stderr only where a pre-existing panic's thread id differs), an addendum is committed and the field is removed, matching round 11. If any output differs, the field stays and a Java-backed pin is requested through the relay instead of being invented.
